departures: Record form: spike/pyodide stays local and its diff goes to the wave branch as docs/design/spikes/pyodide.patch (owner's rule of 2026-11-05, as for the kernel spikes); ADR 0070's choice 3 had the branch pushed.

Cold load (C1) is measured in a persistent Chromium context (a profile on disk, launchPersistentContext with the project's launch options) because Playwright's default context keeps its HTTP cache in memory, where pyodide.asm.wasm (9.6 MB) and the core's wasm (20 MB) are not kept across a reload, so the default context does not meet ADR 0070's 'with Pyodide's files and partsmith.zip in the HTTP cache'. The default-context reload (P-1's way) is recorded too.

The preview server was started by hand with the configuration's exact command (pnpm build && pnpm preview --port 4173 --strictPort) and reused by Playwright (reuseExistingServer outside CI), so the build ended and the load average settled before any timed set; each test ran alone with -g, with /proc/loadavg read before and after.

Every measured call in the worker starts in a new task (08f36b7): Playwright's Worker.evaluate runs code, and the microtasks it queues, with DevTools' exemption from the eval check (shown: eval allowed synchronously and in a microtask inside evaluate, refused with a violation in a new task). The spec adds a control test for it.

The box script's first statement (the import of the already imported package) runs untimed; the time runs from Document() to the return of document.close(), as ADR 0070 says, on the web and natively, by splitting the script's statements with ast; the text run is exactly the box script.

The native box script harness and the per-operation row 2 replica are not on the branch (the branch holds only what ADR 0070 names); their full text is in the Result of docs/adr/0070-pyodide-spike-decides-when-web-scripting-ships.md. Row 2 itself ran as python/tests/test_budgets.py has it.
Pyodide's memory is read through its private _module, as ADR 0070 says; the worker's lint suppression names it.

question_7_files_and_licenses.what_a_deployment_owes: Serving pyodide.mjs (minified), pyodide.asm.mjs and pyodide.asm.wasm is distribution in Executable Form: the deployment must make Pyodide's source at tag 314.0.7 available and tell recipients how to get it, at no more than the cost of distribution (MPL-2.0 3.2(a)); MPL-2.0 is file-level, so Partsmith's own files stay Apache-2.0 (3.3, Larger Work). CPython's PSF license asks that its license agreement and copyright notice be retained in any derivative version, and the MIT, BSD, zlib and bzip2 licenses of the linked libraries and of the bundled JavaScript (StackFrame, ErrorStackParser, MiniLZ4) ask for their notices; the spike's served files carry none. For M4: Pyodide's source at 314.0.7 (and the sources of what it links, at the versions above) in the web deployment's dependency source archives (delivery.md 2.13), entries for Pyodide, CPython, the libraries in pyodide.asm.wasm, Emscripten 5.0.3's runtime (its JavaScript in pyodide.asm.mjs and its system libraries in pyodide.asm.wasm; the notices name only the core's Emscripten 4.0.15 today) and the bundled JavaScript (StackFrame and ErrorStackParser, MIT, Eric Wendelin and other contributors; MiniLZ4, MIT, Pierre Curto) in ui/public/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (delivery.md 2.9), and Pyodide as a production dependency or a name in EMITTED_BUILD_PACKAGES so check:licenses and the notices cover the served files. MPL-2.0 and Python-2.0 are already in deny.toml's allowed list.

question_8_findings_for_m4: Known, confirmed by reading the code: a Python document needs a session of its own with display off and SequentialIds. partsmith-py's Session(display=False, deterministic_ids=True) builds SessionOptions::headless() with SequentialIds per Document; the web core's one session (thread_local in partsmith-wasm) has display on and RandomIdGenerator. The spike's _core.Session ignores both keywords and every Document shares the core instance's session, so the box script's text matched only because the package names the records it adds itself (Document._new_id); a body that import_step adds (and every rectangle and polygon once item 24 lands) would get a random id on the web. Since ps_call has no session parameter, a session per Python document needs a new export or a protocol command that opens a session or document with options (either changes ADR 0010 or the protocol schema), or one core instance per Python document (16,777,216 bytes of WebAssembly memory each at start, measured).

New: with display on, every recompute that Python drives on the web core also tessellates display meshes that the package never reads; part of the 1.48 ms inside callCore of the web box script is that work. The per-document headless session of the first finding removes it.

Known: a script feature that runs during a build needs a call from the core into Python through a JavaScript import, which is unsafe code outside the three exports ADR 0010 allows; it needs a new ADR. The spike's route needs no such call: Python calls the core, never the reverse.

Known, confirmed: Python on the web is 3.14.2 (pyodide-lock.json info.python), beside CPython 3.12.3 for the desktop baseline. The unchanged package imported and ran the box script and row 2 on 3.14.2.

New: two Emscripten runtimes share the worker without conflict: the core (Emscripten 4.0.15, -sENVIRONMENT=worker, MODULARIZE, 16 MiB initial memory) and Pyodide (Emscripten 5.0.3, 30 MiB initial memory). The route needs no change to the core's link arguments.

New: _core.ptsm_schema() and protocol_schema() have no protocol command, so the web _core raises NotImplementedError; no module of python/partsmith calls them (only python/tests/test_core.py and _core.pyi name them), so the package does not need them on the web.

New, not measured: the package reads and writes files through Python's os and pathlib (Document.save, import_step(path), the exports, _files.write_atomic with fsync and os.replace). On Pyodide those reach Emscripten's in-memory file system, not the app's files; M4 must map them (for example Pyodide's mountNativeFS onto the File System Access handles, or bytes in and out through the bridge).

New: the frames cross JavaScript twice per call, Python bytes to a Uint8Array (to_js) and the response back (to_bytes), on top of callCore's two copies; the measured Python overhead, which counts the conversions, stays at 0.14 to 0.56 ms per call (medians), against 0.05 to 0.28 ms natively.

New: the core instance of the spike never receives the page's cancel word (useCancelWord is not called), so a long Python-driven rebuild could not be cancelled; M4 wires the cancel word for Python's core instance if scripts can run long.

Method finding for M4's tests: Playwright's Worker.evaluate, like Page.evaluate, runs its code and the microtasks it queues with DevTools' exemption from the eval check, so a policy test that runs code synchronously inside evaluate cannot see an eval refusal; the spike runs every measured call in a new task and adds a control.
